texts.facts: 4. The applicant herein has approached this Court apprehending arrest in connection with FIR dated 03/07/2019, wherein offences have been registered against him under various provisions of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 as also sections 188, 282, 273 and 328 of the Indian Penal Code. As per reply, a raid was conducted on Taj Pan Masala whereby contraband product namely; pan masala and ghutka amounting to Rs.75,210/- was sei According to reply, at the time of raid, applicant was present on the spot. Prima facie, stock of pan masala cannot attract the provisions of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code. Since, applicant has joined the investigation, in my view, custodial presence of applicant is not at all necessary.
texts.arguments: 5. It is pointed out by the learned counsel for the applicant that barring section 328 of the Indian KHUNTE aba532.19.odt Penal code, all the offences are bailable. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that although contraband material i.e. Pan Masala was recovered from premises with which the applicant could be connected, there was no prima facie material to connect Alla Rakha Abdul Gaffar vs State Of Maharashtra, Thr. It was further pointed out that section 328 of the Indian Penal Code could not have been invoked in the facts of the present case.
